title: My body, my health
cando: say how you feel and where it hurts, and ask for help

about.text: This lesson is about your body. You say where it hurts. You ask for help.
goals: Say where it hurts: My head hurts.
Say how you feel: I'm ill. I'm tired.
Ask for help: Can you help me?
Read an “If you need help” sign.
Write a short note for the doctor.

chapters.title: With the doctor
chapters.text:
This lesson is about your health.
First, Kwame is ill. He is with the doctor.
The doctor asks: Where does it hurt?
Kwame says: My head hurts. And my back.
Then he asks: Can you help me?

chapters.title: My head hurts
chapters.text:
Where does it hurt? Say my, a body part, and hurts.
My head hurts. My back hurts.
For two feet, say: My feet hurt.
For how you feel, say I am. I am ill. I am tired.
Do not say: I have tired.

chapters.title: A sign and a note
chapters.text:
Next, you read a sign. It is for ill people.
It says: Ill? Tell the desk your name.
Then you write a note. It is for the doctor.
Say how you feel. Say where it hurts.

chapters.title: Ask for help
chapters.text:
Then you are at work. You feel ill.
Tell someone. Say where it hurts.
Then ask: Can you call a doctor, please?

chapters.title: The book
chapters.text:
Last, you read a short story. It is about health.
Read it once for the story. Then read it again.

warmup.prompt: You feel ill at work. What do you do first?
warmup.note: There is no wrong answer. But tell someone. People want to help.

conversation.title: Where does it hurt?
conversation.setting: Kwame is ill. He is with the doctor.
lines: Oh dear. Where does it hurt?
My head hurts. And my back.
Two days. Can you help me?
Yes, of course. Stay in bed today.
Can I go to work tomorrow?
No. Stay at home for two days.

questions.why: Kwame says: My head hurts. And my back.
Kwame says: I'm ill. I'm very tired.

questions.a: Stay at home for two days.
questions.why: The doctor says: Stay at home for two days.

phrases.use: A question when you meet someone.
An answer when you are not well.
When someone tells you bad news.

items.meaning: All of you, from head to feet.
The top part of your body. Your eyes are there.
You have two. Your hand is at the end.
items.example: My arm hurts. I can't work.

items.meaning: At the end of your arm. You write with it.
items.example: My hand hurts. I can't write.

items.meaning: You walk on them. You have two.
items.example: My leg hurts. I can't walk.

items.meaning: At the end of your leg. Two of them are feet.
items.example: My foot hurts in these shoes.

items.meaning: You see with it. You have two.
The part of your body behind you.
You eat with it. More than one: teeth.
items.example: My tooth hurts. I can't eat.

items.meaning: A part of your body is bad. You feel it.
Not well. Your body is not OK.
items.example: I'm ill today. I can't go to work.

items.meaning: You want to sleep or sit down.

sound.title: hurt and heart
sound.explain: Hurt and heart are not the same. Hurt has the sound in her and work. Heart has the sound in arm and father. Listen, then say each group.
lines: Put your hand on your heart.

sayIt.instructions: Say Kwame's lines. Record yourself, then listen back. Is your voice clear?
lines: My head hurts. And my back.
Two days. Can you help me?

spot.instructions: Look at these sentences from the conversation.
spot.question: Which one says where it hurts? Which two say how Kwame feels? Which one asks for help?
spot.answer: My + a part of the body + hurts: my head hurts. I am + how you feel: I'm ill. I'm very tired. Can you help me? asks for help.

rules.title: How you feel, and where it hurts
rule: My + part of the body + hurts: My head hurts. My back hurts.
Two feet, two eyes: My feet hurt. My eyes hurt.
I am + how you feel: I am ill. I am tired.
Ask for help: Can you help me, please?
The doctor asks: Where does it hurt?
rules.mistake: Not: I have tired. Say: I am tired. Not: My head hurt. Say: My head hurts.

practice.why: My head is one part, so hurts, with s.
Two feet, so hurt, with no s.
I am + how you feel: I am tired.
Omar is one person, so he is ill.
Can you help me? asks for help.
The doctor asks: Where does it hurt?

practice.why: You see with your eyes. Two eyes, so hurt.

yourTurn.prompt: You are ill today. Say how you feel and where it hurts. Then ask for help. Write three or four short lines.

text.title: If you need help
text.body:
PRACTICE SIGN: not a real centre

GREENWAY HEALTH CENTRE
Open 8 to 6

IF YOU NEED HELP
Ill? Tell the desk your name.
Then sit and wait.
Very ill? Tell the desk now.
Can't walk? Ask for help.

At night, call 01632 960 418.
The hospital is on Station Road.

liveClass: Day 1: point and name. Each learner points to a part of the body and says it. Then practise the doctor conversation in pairs, and change the part that hurts.
Day 2: the real-life task. You are someone at work. Each learner says they feel ill, says where it hurts, and asks you to call a doctor.
Day 3: talk about the book. Then two learners read their notes for the doctor aloud.
